paradoxes.text: The grid sold to ease the debt ties the debt to China: critics read the 2020 transfer of 90% of EDL-T for USD 600m as debt-for-equity, and the payment was expected to go to debts owed to Chinese creditors (not confirmed), while the Chinese partner now shares in the transmission revenue that EDL's finances depend on.

grand_strategy.reading: Laos is a landlocked one-party state whose main asset is water: its dams sell power to Vietnam, and the high-voltage grid that carries it is now majority-controlled through a Chinese company, the price of a debt that the IMF still treats as distressed. Its policy is to hold the Vietnamese special relationship as the political anchor and to spread its partners so that none of them sets its choices. The record reserves of 2026 buy time; they do not solve the debt.

stances.note: Ally by the Lao side's own statements: President Thongloun in Hanoi (26-27 Jan 2026) and To Lam in Vientiane (5 Feb 2026) reaffirmed the 'special relationship' and a 'strategic partnership', with party plans for 2026-2030 and six documents. No collective defence. Laos sells power and Vietnam gives the sea outlet (Vung Ang). The 1977 date comes from the Wikipedia index (pointer only). Bond affinity: two one-party states (our reading).
